title: Agent-assisted project planning and UI discovery
context: Planning only. Use Codex to interview, research unfamiliar tools, define the Next.js system, learn frontend terminology, explore live component sources, and deliver a decision-complete build plan without writing production application code.

stories.title: Run the Codex product-planning interview
stories.outcome: The raw client idea becomes an explicit set of facts, preferences, assumptions, unknowns, and decisions.
stories.context: Provide the ClearPath brief and discovery notes. Instruct Codex not to implement and to ask one material question at a time.
acceptanceCriteria: Interview covers user, outcome, workflow, scope, non-goals, data, integrations, budget, content, design, operations, and success
Facts, preferences, assumptions, unknowns, and decisions are separated
Material unanswered questions are escalated rather than invented

expectations.security: No real client secrets or private data.
expectations.analytics: Success metrics defined without sensitive data.

stories.title: Research the Next.js delivery options
stories.outcome: The system plan uses current tools for a stated reason and rejects unnecessary complexity.
stories.context: Ask Codex to research current official documentation for Next.js, Vercel, form/email delivery, analytics, testing, and UI foundations. Compare library/service/build alternatives.
acceptanceCriteria: Decision matrix links primary docs and records current compatibility
Every option covers purpose, cost/limit, security/data boundary, maintenance, lock-in, and rejection reason
Browser, Next.js server, external service, and deployment responsibilities are diagrammed
At least one novel Codex recommendation is verified and one is rejected
stories.dataContract: Architecture/tool decision matrix and system diagram.

expectations.accessibility: Tool choice does not waive accessibility.

definitionOfDone: Decisions have evidence and reversal triggers

stories.title: Build a visual frontend vocabulary
stories.outcome: You can name common UI patterns and specify your intent precisely to Codex.
stories.context: Use live component documentation and the UI field guide. Capture at least thirty terms with a visual example, purpose, and misuse case.
acceptanceCriteria: Glossary covers layout, navigation, content, forms, feedback, overlays, data display, responsive, tokens, states, and motion
Every term has a direct live example and plain-language definition
You can identify ten randomly selected patterns from screenshots and explain their role
stories.dataContract: Visual glossary with links/screenshots and text alternatives.

expectations.accessibility: Images have text explanation; patterns include keyboard/state behavior.

stories.title: Select and audit the component sources
stories.outcome: ClearPath has one coherent UI foundation and a small justified specialist shortlist.
stories.context: Explore shadcn/ui, Radix, Base UI, React Aria, Aceternity UI, Magic UI, 21st.dev, and Motion visually. Select one foundation and at most two specialist components for later implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: Every considered source has direct link, role, license, version fit, install model, dependencies, accessibility, mobile/reduced-motion, and maintenance notes
One foundation is selected for behavior/consistency
At most two specialist components are shortlisted and mapped to user/story value
Rejected sources include reasons

expectations.security: Third-party source will be reviewed before installation.
expectations.privacy: No data concerns at planning stage.

nonGoals: Mixing multiple primitive systems for the same control

stories.title: Turn an ambiguous request into a visual agency story
stories.outcome: A fresh Codex implementation task can understand one ClearPath outcome, boundary, and proof without inventing product decisions.
stories.context: Use Codex to interview you about one vague client request, then create and critique an implementation-ready Markdown story with the agency template and the smallest useful Mermaid visual.
acceptanceCriteria: The story separates facts, preferences, assumptions, unknowns, and decisions
The story is a demonstrable vertical user outcome rather than separate frontend, backend, and database tasks
Happy-path and failure-path acceptance examples are observable Given/When/Then behavior
Data/API, security, privacy, accessibility, analytics, dependencies, non-goals, Definition of Done, and evidence are explicit
Every Mermaid diagram renders, uses text labels in addition to color, and has an equivalent plain-text route
A Codex multi-role critique is answered and the final Markdown diff contains no invented client fact
stories.dataContract: One Markdown agency story using the supplied template, including validated Mermaid when a visual materially improves understanding.

expectations.security: Threats, authorization, and credential boundaries appear when relevant; no real client data enters the prompt.
expectations.privacy: Minimum data and third-party sharing are explicit.
expectations.accessibility: Acceptance covers keyboard, focus, semantics, errors, responsive behavior, and diagram text alternatives.
expectations.analytics: Events connect to the stated outcome and exclude sensitive values.

nonGoals: Generating the entire backlog in one prompt
definitionOfDone: A fresh Codex task accurately restates the story and identifies no material unanswered implementation decision
Markdown lint and Mermaid rendering pass
You defend the slice and acceptance examples without reading generated prose

stories.title: Approve the implementation-ready plan and design direction
stories.outcome: Milestone 3 can begin without unresolved product, technical, or visual decisions that would change the build.
stories.context: Present three genuinely different design directions, score them, select one, then convert the project into epics/stories with acceptance and test evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: PRD, journey, sitemap, system diagram, decisions, risks, non-goals, visual stories, and story map agree
Three visual directions differ in hierarchy/style, not only color
Chosen direction defines tokens, components, states, responsive behavior, motion, and source audit
Codex red-team review is answered and material open decisions are resolved or explicitly spiked
Markdown lint and Mermaid rendering pass
No production app code was written

expectations.accessibility: Critical states and keyboard behavior specified.
